title: codeanalyzer Neo4j graph contract
description: Meta-schema for the schema.neo4j.json document each codeanalyzer emits with `--emit schema`. The document describes the graph an analyzer writes — node labels, relationship types, and the constraints and indexes the loader creates — so it is a contract about a graph, not a JSON Schema for analysis.json. Its schema_version is an independent line from the analysis schema version: an analyzer can sit on analysis schema v1 while its graph contract is on 2.x.

x-cldk.note: The copies under neo4j/<lang>/ are byte-identical to the tagged release, so `diff` against the analyzer repo is the drift check. They are pinned to the latest release, not to whatever sits on main.

schema_version.description: Version of the graph contract itself, independent of the analysis schema version.

generator.description: Analyzer that emitted this contract, e.g. codeanalyzer-java.

marker_labels.description: Extra labels attached to nodes that satisfy some property (e.g. JEntrypoint), rather than to a node kind.

constraints.description: Cypher CREATE CONSTRAINT statements the loader runs before ingest.

indexes.description: Cypher CREATE INDEX statements the loader runs before ingest.

label.description: Neo4j label written on the node.

merge_label.description: Label used in the MERGE that upserts the node, when it differs from `label`. Java and Python spell this merge_label; TypeScript spells it mergeLabel. Either is accepted here — the divergence is real in the shipped contracts.

mergeLabel.description: TypeScript's spelling of merge_label. See the note on merge_label.

key.description: Property that uniquely identifies a node with this label.

properties.description: Property name to property type. Values are contract type names, not JSON Schema types.

type.description: Relationship type written on the edge, e.g. PY_HAS_MODULE.

from.description: Node labels this edge may start at.

to.description: Node labels this edge may end at.

PropertyType.description: Contract-level property type. This is the set the three shipped contracts use; extend it when an analyzer starts emitting a new one.
